gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's 350 W panel, sold on BLUETTI's US store as the Elite 200 V2 + 2×350W kit ($2,148), has a 33 V open-circuit voltage, so two in series reach 66 V. That is over the Elite 200 V2's 60 V solar-input limit, so the kit's panels cannot be wired in series. BLUETTI's own 200 W panel (24.6 V) can take a two-panel series string (49.2 V).
standout_why: I compared against four pages. powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (cited) lists the Elite 200 V2 at 12–60 V, 20 A, XT60, does the series-voltage arithmetic only for Jackery SolarSaga panels, and covers only the Elite 200 V2 + 200W kit. theoutagebrief.com (cited) gives wattage caps only (Jackery 2000 v2 400 W, not expandable; DELTA 2 Max 1,000 W; C2000 Gen 2 800 W) with no voltage, connector or panel-pairing limits. generatorandbackup.com (cited) says DELTA 2 Max is 'expandable to 6 kWh' without naming the battery, and gives no voltage, connector or panel-pairing limits for the Elite 200 V2. unpluggedwatts.com (cited) could not be read: TLS certificate error. None of them checks the Voc of the panels inside BLUETTI's bundles against the station's 60 V limit, and none mentions the 350 W bundles.
decides: This confirms the pick, not overturns it: for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, the 2×200W kit ($1,499, BLUETTI store, 2026-11-08) is the bundle whose panels can go in series within the station's 60 V limit. The 2×350W kit costs $649 more, and BLUETTI's US kit and panel pages list no parallel connector for it. They list one 20 A MC4-to-XT60 cable per 350 W panel. For EcoFlow, the store names the DELTA 2 Max's expansion battery (up to two DELTA 2 Max Smart Extra Batteries, 6,144 Wh), which supports ChatGPT's 'best for expansion' label. EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Max series text lists '2–10kWh expandable' and Smart Generator pairing only under DELTA 3 Max Plus. Also, ChatGPT's '$1,429 DELTA 3 Max' price matches EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Max Plus Solar Generator listing; the plain DELTA 3 Max Solar Generator is $1,249.

findings.product: BLUETTI 350W Solar Panel (in Elite 200 V2 + 350W / 2×350W kits)
findings.label: Open-circuit voltage and fit with Elite 200 V2
findings.value: 33 V Voc per panel; 2 in series = 66 V, above the Elite 200 V2's 60 V limit
findings.note: Page states '33V open-circuit voltage (Voc)', MC4 connectors, and one 20A MC4-to-XT60 cable (1.5 m) per panel. No parallel or Y connector is listed. Elite 200 V2 is on its compatible-station list. Arithmetic: 2 × 33 V = 66 V > 60 V. The single 350W panel page (https://www.bluettipower.com/products/350w-solar-panel) gives the same 33 V. The US kit URL slug is 'pv350d'.
